title: Finite pro-etale smooth base change
statement:
Use the finite coefficient conventions [sbc-def-coefficient-conventions]: $\Lambda$ is a finite discrete commutative ring, $N\geq1$, $(N:\Lambda)=0$, and $N$ is invertible on $S$. Let
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
Y&\xrightarrow{e}&T\\
h\downarrow&&\downarrow g\\
X&\xrightarrow{f}&S
\end{array}
$$
be a cartesian square [sbc-def-base-change-square] of noetherian schemes (each admits a finite affine open cover by spectra of rings in which every ideal is finitely generated), with $f$ smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and $g$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. On every pro-etale corner $W$, use the constant coefficient ring $\Lambda_{W,\Proet}$ and the category $\Dbc(W_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with the canonical structure isomorphisms of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Use the ordinary, uncompleted operations [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For every $K\in\Dbc(T_{\Proet},\Lambda)$, the canonical ambient ringed exchange [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]
$$
F_K:Lf^*_{\Proet}Rg_{*,\Proet}K\longrightarrow Rh_{*,\Proet}Le^*_{\Proet}K
$$
is an isomorphism in $D(X_{\Proet},\Lambda)$. For any etale model $L\in\Dbc(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and isomorphism $\alpha:\nu_T^*L\cong K$ supplied by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], where $\nu^*$ is [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], it is obtained by conjugating the canonical etale exchange isomorphism of [sbc-thm-bounded-derived-smooth-base-change] by the canonical site-comparison isomorphisms and $\alpha$. No boundedness or constructibility of either endpoint is asserted.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], membership of $K$ in $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ supplies an etale bounded constructible complex $L$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:\nu_T^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. Its cohomology vanishes outside some finite interval $[a,b]$, so in particular $L\in\Dplus(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$. Fix this model for the remainder of the proof. No inference from a system of coefficient reductions, and no essential-surjectivity assertion for arbitrary pro-etale complexes, is needed.

source.place: Definition of Dbc as the essential image of bounded constructible etale complexes; finite-coefficient clarification in the reviewed DAG statement

proof.text: Apply [sbc-thm-bounded-derived-smooth-base-change] to $L$ on this square. All its hypotheses are present: $\Lambda$ is finite commutative, the positive annihilator $N$ is invertible on $S$, $f$ is smooth, $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $L$ is bounded constructible. Thus the specified etale module exchange $E_L: f_{\Et}^{-1}Rg_{\Et,*}L\to Rh_{\Et,*}e_{\Et}^{-1}L$ is an isomorphism in the ambient derived category. Here [sbc-def-base-change-map] identifies exact constant-coefficient pullback with inverse image and explicitly specifies that the bounded-below restriction uses the same module unit--square--counit mate formula. Consequently $E_L$ is the etale module exchange appearing in the transport lemma below, under the canonical bounded-below/ambient identifications; it is not an arbitrary isomorphism of its endpoints.

proof.text:
Since $h$ is the base change of $g$, clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes $h$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. We may therefore use [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] on both $g$ and $h$, and [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] on $f$ and $e$. Use their canonical derived module versions with precisely the counit-mate normalization stated in [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange]. In the notation of that lemma, $A_W=\nu_W^*$, $a_u:A_Uu_{\Et}^{-1}\cong Lu_{\Proet}^*A_V$ and $b_u:A_VRu_{\Et,*}\cong Ru_{\Proet,*}A_U$. It supplies the following isomorphisms with their specified components:
$$
\begin{split}
S_L&=Lf_{\Proet}^*(b_{g,L})\circ a_{f,Rg_{\Et,*}L}:
 A_X(f_{\Et}^{-1}Rg_{\Et,*}L)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf_{\Proet}^*Rg_{\Proet,*}A_TL,\\
T_L&=Rh_{\Proet,*}(a_{e,L})\circ b_{h,e_{\Et}^{-1}L}:
 A_X(Rh_{\Et,*}e_{\Et}^{-1}L)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_{\Proet,*}Le_{\Proet}^*A_TL.
\end{split}
$$
Only the input $L$ is required to be bounded below. We do not require the two exchange endpoints to be bounded constructible.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange] with its corners $(X,Y,X',Y')$ renamed $(T,S,Y,X)$ and its edges $(f,f',g,g')$ renamed $(g,h,f,e)$. The coefficient ring is finite discrete commutative, the two vertical edges $g,h$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by step 3, and $L\in D^+$ by step 1. Its equality is exactly
$$
 T_L\circ\nu_X^*(E_L)=F_{\nu_T^*L}\circ S_L.
$$
In particular the pro-etale map on the right is the canonical ambient ringed exchange, with the stated constant-ring structure maps. Multiplying on the right by $S_L^{-1}$ gives
$$F_{\nu_T^*L}=T_L\circ\nu_X^*(E_L)\circ S_L^{-1}.$$
A functor sends the inverse of an isomorphism to the inverse of its image. Step 2 therefore makes the middle factor invertible, and all three factors in this displayed formula are isomorphisms. This proves the claim at the chosen etale model with the required conjugation identity.

source.place: Conjugation identity T_L A(E_L)=Ex S_L; the explicit inverse/cancellation is elementary

proof.text:
The exchange of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] is a natural transformation on the ambient pro-etale derived category. Its naturality at $\alpha:\nu_T^*L\cong K$ states
$$
 Rh_{\Proet,*}Le_{\Proet}^*(\alpha)\circ F_{\nu_T^*L}
 =F_K\circ Lf_{\Proet}^*Rg_{\Proet,*}(\alpha).
$$
Both functor images of $\alpha$ are isomorphisms: their inverses are the images of $\alpha^{-1}$. Thus
$$
F_K=Rh_{\Proet,*}Le_{\Proet}^*(\alpha)\circ T_L\circ\nu_X^*(E_L)\circ S_L^{-1}\circ
 \bigl(Lf_{\Proet}^*Rg_{\Proet,*}(\alpha)\bigr)^{-1}.
$$
Every factor is invertible by step 4 and the preceding inverse calculation. This proves both the asserted isomorphism and the stated description for every choice of the etale model.
